results.name: Chest Dip Weighted Slow
instructions: Grip the dip bars firmly with your palms facing inward and your arms fully extended. Position your body slightly forward, with your legs bent and crossed at the ankles, holding weights.
Slowly lower your body by bending your elbows, allowing them to flare out slightly to the sides. Lower yourself in a controlled manner until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Push through your palms to slowly extend your elbows and lift your body back to the starting position. Maintain the forward lean throughout the movement to keep the focus on your chest muscles.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining a slow and controlled pace throughout the exercise.
tips: Ensure your body remains slightly forward to maximize chest activation and minimize strain on your shoulders.
Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form and control.
Perform both the lowering and lifting phases slowly to increase muscle engagement and control.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement; maintain a slight bend to keep tension on your muscles.
results.description: Chest Dip Weighted Slow is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Chest Dip With Pause Bodyweight
instructions: Begin by grasping the parallel bars with your palms facing inward and your arms fully extended to lift your body off the floor and lean slightly forward, crossing your ankles behind you for balance.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor, keeping your chest leaning forward to engage your chest muscles.

Push through your palms to extend your elbows and lift your body back to the starting position. Pause in the upper position for a few seconds, allowing for a couple seconds of rest. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on leaning forward slightly to emphasize the chest muscles rather than the triceps.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement to maintain tension on your muscles.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to prevent unnecessary strain.
results.description: Chest Dip With Pause Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Chest Fly High to Low Resistance Band
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a low anchor point behind you. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding a handle in each hand with your palms facing up.
Position one leg forward and the other back, with both knees slightly bent, keeping your back straight and your arms extended down and slightly behind you.
Raise the handles up and together in a wide arc, bringing them to meet at head level while keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you raise the handles and inhale as you lower them back down.
Use a lighter resistance band if needed to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on squeezing your upper chest muscles at the top of the movement.
results.description: Chest Fly High to Low Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Chest Fly Low to High Resistance Band
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a high anchor point behind you. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding a handle in each hand with your palms facing forward.
Position one leg forward and the other back, with both knees slightly bent. Keep your back straight and your arms extended out to the sides at head height.
Bring the handles down and together in a wide arc, meeting in front of your lower abdomen while keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly raise your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you raise the handles and inhale as you lower them back down.
Use a lighter resistance band if needed to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on squeezing your upper chest muscles at the top of the movement.
results.description: Chest Fly Low to High Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Chest Press Front Resistance Band
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point behind you at chest height. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding a handle in each hand with your palms facing down.
Position one leg forward and the other back, with both knees slightly bent. Start with your elbows bent at 90 degrees, your hands at chest level, and your arms parallel to the floor.
Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly return to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you push the handles forward and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Maintain a neutral wrist position to prevent strain.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Chest Press Front Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Chest Press Low to High Resistance Band
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a low anchor point behind you. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding a handle in each hand with your palms facing down.
Position one leg forward and the other back, with both knees slightly bent. Start with your elbows bent and your hands close to your chest sides.
Push the handles forward and up in a diagonal motion until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly return to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you push the handles forward and down, and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Keep your back straight and avoid using momentum.
Focus on engaging your upper chest muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Chest Press Low to High Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Chest Press Machine
instructions: Sit down on the chest press machine with your feet flat on the floor and your back pressed firmly against the backrest. Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing forward, and position your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Push the handles forward and extend your arms fully, keeping a slight bend in your elbows to avoid locking them.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbows and bringing the handles back towards your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back and head flat against the backrest to maintain proper form.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you push the handles forward and inhale as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Chest Press Machine is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Chest Press Decline
instructions: Lie on a decline bench with your feet securely placed under the footpads. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended above your chest, palms facing forward.
Lower the dumbbells slowly towards your chest by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Push the dumbbells back to the starting position by straightening your arms, squeezing your chest at the top of the movement.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the exercise.
tips: Ensure your feet are securely positioned under the footpads to prevent slipping during the movement.
Maintain a steady and controlled motion, avoiding any jerking or sudden movements.
Breathe in as you lower the dumbbells and exhale as you press them back up.
results.description: Dumbbell Chest Press Decline is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Chest Pull Over
instructions: Lie crosswise on a bench, with your upper back and shoulders supported, feet firmly planted on the floor and hips slightly lowered. Hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest, arms slightly bent.
Slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head and down towards the floor, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Bring the dumbbell back up to the starting position by reversing the arc motion, focusing on engaging your chest and lats.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the exercise.
tips: Keep a firm grip on the dumbbell to maintain control and prevent it from slipping.
Avoid lowering the dumbbell too far to prevent shoulder strain.
Engage your core to stabilize your body and support your lower back.
results.description: Dumbbell Chest Pull Over is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.
